sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The **Quit India Movement** (August Kranti), **Azad Hind Fauj (INA)**, and the revolutionary leadership of **Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose** representing the final aggressive phase of the Indian freedom struggle.
Quit India Movement launched on **8 August 1942**; INA organized in **1942** and reorganized by Netaji in **1943**.
Quit India spanned across **All India** (headquartered in Bombay); INA operations spanned **Singapore, Malaya, Burma (Myanmar), and Andaman & Nicobar**.

**Mahatma Gandhi** (Quit India slogan 'Do or Die'), **Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose** (Azad Hind Fauj leader, 'Delhi Chalo', 'Give me blood and I will give you freedom'), **Ras Behari Bose** (Founder of INA/League), **Aruna Asaf Ali** (Hoisted Congress flag).
Marked the mass civil disobedience of the masses and armed resistance by the military, shaking the foundations of the **British Empire** and forcing post-war withdrawal.
Leaderless movement due to immediate arrest of top leaders, parallel governments (**Prati Sarkar** in Satara, Ballia, Tamluk), women's regiment (**Jhansi Regiment** under Captain Lakshmi Sahgal).
High-scoring static GK area covering exact dates, slogans, founders, parallel government locations, and trial details of INA officers (**Red Fort Trials**).
**Linlithgow** was the Viceroy during Quit India; **Clement Attlee** was the British PM when India gained independence following these uprisings.

items.title: 1. Cripps Mission (1942) and Background to Quit India
items.content:
• **Staford Cripps** sent to India in **March 1942** to secure Indian cooperation for WWII.
• Proposed **Dominion status** after the war and right of provinces to secede (rejected by Congress).
• Mahatma Gandhi termed it a **'post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'**.
• Failure of Cripps Mission led directly to the call for the **Quit India Movement**.
• **Mnemonic:** **C**ripps **C**rashed like a **C**racked **C**heque in **42**.

items.title: 2. Launch of Quit India Movement (August Kranti)
items.content:
• Passed on **8 August 1942** at the **Gowalia Tank Maidan (Bombay)** session of the All India Congress Committee (AICC).
• Mahatma Gandhi gave the famous slogan: **'Do or Die' (Karenge ya Marenge)**.
• Operation **Zero Hour**: British arrested all major leaders (Gandhi, Nehru, Patel, Azad) in the early hours of **9 August 1942**.
• Movement became leaderless, unleashing spontaneous public fury, strikes, and attacks on government symbols.
• **Mnemonic:** **8**th August = **A**ugust **K**ranti (**AK-42** - August Kranti, 1942).

items.title: 3. Parallel Governments during Quit India
items.content:
• **Ballia (Uttar Pradesh):** Led by **Chittu Pandey**, overthrew district administration and freed Congress leaders.
• **Tamluk (Midnapore, Bengal):** **Jatiya Sarkar** formed, active till September 1944, had its own Vidyut Vahini.
• **Satara (Maharashtra):** **Prati Sarkar** led by **Nana Patil** and Y.B. Chavan; lasted the longest (till 1945), had village libraries and justice courts.
• Highlighted robust grassroots organization despite British repression.

items.title: 4. Formation and Growth of Azad Hind Fauj (INA)
items.content:
• Originally conceived by **Mohan Singh** in **1942** out of Indian POWs captured by Japan in Malaya.
• Revamped by **Ras Behari Bose**, who handed over leadership to **Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose** in **July 1943** in Singapore.
• Netaji formed the Provisional Government of Free India (**Arzi Hukumat-e-Azad Hind**) on **21 October 1943**.
• Armed forces included regiments named after Gandhi, Nehru, Azad, and a women's regiment named **Rani Jhansi Regiment** led by **Captain Lakshmi Sahgal**.
• **Mnemonic:** **M**ohan started, **R**as expanded, **N**etaji commanded (**MRN**).

items.title: 5. Netaji's Slogans and Military Campaign
items.content:
• **'Delhi Chalo'** (On to Delhi) given in Singapore in 1943.
• **'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!'** (Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azadi doonga).
• INA headquarters shifted to **Rangoon (Myanmar)**.
• INA captured **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, renaming them **Shahid Dweep** and **Swaraj Dweep**.
• INA hoisted the tricolor flag at **Moirang (Manipur)** on Indian soil in March 1944.

items.title: 6. INA Trials and Post-War Upheaval (1945-1946)
items.content:
• Following the defeat of Japan in WWII, INA soldiers were captured and put on public trial at the **Red Fort (Delhi)** in **1945**.
• Prominent defendants: **P.K. Sehgal, Shah Nawaz Khan, and Gurbakhsh Singh Dhillon**.
• Defense lawyers organized by Congress included **Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Asaf Ali**.
• Led to massive nationwide protests, naval mutiny (**RIN Mutiny** in Bombay, Feb 1946), hastening the British exit from India.

sections.title: Comprehensive Data Tables
rows: Sent by Churchill; offered Dominion status post-war; rejected by Indian leaders as inadequate.
Passed at Gowalia Tank, Bombay; gave 'Do or Die' call under Gandhi's leadership.
Pre-dawn crackdown by British arresting all top INC leaders to paralyze the movement.
Founded by Captain Mohan Singh with Japanese support using Indian POWs.
Subhash Chandra Bose arrived in Singapore from Germany via submarine; took supreme command.
Provisional Government of Free India formed in Singapore; recognized by Axis powers.
INA hoisted Indian flag at Moirang, Manipur, entering mainland India.
Public trials of INA officers at Red Fort, Delhi; triggered massive anti-British solidarity.
Royal Indian Navy mutiny in Bombay; final nail in the coffin for British rule.
Elected Congress President defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya; later resigned and founded Forward Bloc.

items.definition: Remember **'8 is Debate, 9 is Arrest'**. On 8th August, the resolution was debated and passed; on 9th August, leaders were arrested.
Remember **'MRN'** -> **M**ohan Singh (Founder) -> **R**as Behari Bose (Organizer) -> **N**etaji Subhash Chandra Bose (Supreme Commander).
Remember **'BST'** -> **B**allia (Chittu Pandey) -> **S**atara (Nana Patil) -> **T**amluk (Jatiya Sarkar). Uttar Pradesh exam aspirants must prioritize **Ballia** as it is in UP.
Remember **'D-B-D'** -> **D**elhi Chalo (Slogan) -> **B**ose called 'Father of the Nation' to Gandhi first (1944) -> **D**eath mystery in plane crash (1945).

items.term: Trick 5: Red Fort Trial Defence Lawyers
items.definition: Remember **'B-T-J-A'** -> **B**hulabhai Desai, **T**ej Bahadur Sapru, **J**awaharlal Nehru, **A**saf Ali.
Remember **'SS'** -> Andaman renamed **S**hahid Dweep, Nicobar renamed **S**waraj Dweep.
Students often confuse **Captain Mohan Singh** (original founder in 1942) with **Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose** (who took command in 1943). Ras Behari Bose handed over the charge to Netaji.

items.term: Mistake 2: Date of Quit India Movement
items.definition: Do not confuse the resolution date (**8 August 1942**) with the actual mass crackdown date (**9 August 1942**). Exam questions frequently test both.
Remember that **Lord Linlithgow** was the Viceroy during the Quit India Movement in 1942, NOT Lord Wavell (who came in 1943).
Students often think Gandhi was Congress President in 1942. **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** was the Congress President from 1940 to 1945 (longest tenure).

items.term: Mistake 5: Origin of Azad Hind Fauj
items.definition: INA was formed outside India (**Singapore/Malaya**) with Japanese backing, NOT inside British India by underground activists.
Subhash Chandra Bose founded the **Forward Bloc** in **1939** after resigning from the Congress presidency at the Tripuri session, NOT during the Quit India Movement.
The failure of the **Cripps Mission (1942)** paved the way for the ultimate confrontation between Indian nationalists and British authorities.
The **Quit India Resolution** was passed on **8 August 1942** at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, with the historic **'Do or Die'** mantra.
Operation Zero Hour on **9 August 1942** arrested all top leaders, transforming the movement into a massive leaderless public uprising.
Provisional parallel governments were successfully established in **Ballia (UP)**, **Tamluk (Bengal)**, and **Satara (Bombay)**.
Prominent women leaders like **Aruna Asaf Ali**, **Usha Mehta** (underground radio), and **Matangini Hazra** played stellar roles.
Subhash Chandra Bose made a dramatic escape (**Mahabhinishkraman**) from British surveillance in India to Germany in **1941**.
Netaji took over the command of **Azad Hind Fauj (INA)** in **Singapore (1943)** from Ras Behari Bose.
Netaji established the **Arzi Hukumat-e-Azad Hind** on **21 October 1943**, declaring war on Britain and the US.
An all-women combat regiment was formed in INA, named **Rani Jhansi Regiment** under **Captain Lakshmi Sahgal**.
The **Red Fort Trials of 1945** created unprecedented national sympathy and unity, uniting Congress, Muslim League, and the public.
The **Royal Indian Navy Mutiny (February 1946)** demonstrated that the British could no longer rely on Indian armed forces to retain control.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize the exact dates and locations of parallel governments (Ballia, Satara, Tamluk), as direct factual questions frequently appear from this sub-topic.
Do not confuse Captain Mohan Singh (initial creator of INA in 1942) with Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose (who took command in Singapore in 1943). Examiners test this distinction regularly.
Remember Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was the Congress President during the 1942 Quit India Movement and held office continuously from 1940 to 1945.

Avoid the trap that Quit India was a non-violent movement. While Gandhi preached non-violence, the movement witnessed widespread violence, sabotage, and railway track destruction due to immediate leader arrests.

keyTakeaways: Quit India Movement was launched on **8 August 1942** at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, with Gandhi's **'Do or Die'** call.
**Lord Linlithgow** was the British Viceroy during the Quit India Movement.
Parallel governments (**Prati Sarkar**) were formed in Ballia (UP), Tamluk (Bengal), and Satara (Maharashtra).
Azad Hind Fauj (INA) was founded by **Captain Mohan Singh** and later commanded by **Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose** in 1943.
Netaji gave famous slogans like **'Delhi Chalo'** and **'Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azadi doonga'**.
The **Red Fort Trials (1945)** of INA officers rallied national support and hastened India's independence.
The **Rani Jhansi Regiment** was the all-women combat wing of the INA led by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal.
